contexts.text: The women (of the Antediluvians) wear a round black hat, as it were turreted in front. SE 3589.
The covering of the head of those who call themselves saints (in Jupiter) is a turreted hat of a dark colour.
All articles of clothing derive their signification from the part of the body which they cover; as for instance... that which covers the head, as the mitre, the turban, the hat.
Those of them who by machinations, arts, and cunning have come to honours and riches, become magicians there; they appear... sitting at a table with a hat depressed to the eyebrows...
Endowed with the hat of the doctorship.

The life in their eyes was from the perception of truth, and the zeal in their discourse from the affection of truth; on which account hats had been given them from Heaven, the borders of which were ornamented with bands of golden threads interwoven with pearls. TCR. AR 113.
On their heads were curled boat hats... We entered the house of one of the great men, on whose head was a turreted hat.
He gave those who sat on the south hats, the borders of which were ornamented with bands of gold and pearls, and on the left side with diamond elevations cut in the form of flowers.
On the head (of the devil) was a square hat depressed down to his eyes.
She wove a garland of roses... and placed it on the boy's cap... and said. Receive the delights of intelligence; know that a cap signifies intelligence...
Each youth, when he ascended the chair, put on... a hat on the top of which was a rosary encircled with small sapphires.
Distinguished with hats of the doctorship...

I saw a number congregated with hats on their heads; some with hats bound with silk, who were of the ecclesiastical order; some with hats the borders of which were adorned with bands of gold, who were of the civil order; all were learned; and I saw some with turbans, who were not learned.
Those in hats understood and approved; but those in turbans denied.
On hearing these words those who wore hats went away with their hats under their arms, praising God; for in that World the intelligent wear hats. Not so those who wore turbans; for they were bald...
A man started up... who had a turban on his head, and a hat over it; and he touched the hat with his finger, and said...
He wore a hat or cap - mössa mössa... they are known. [NCBS: Swedenborg used the Swedish word mössa here, instead of Latin.]
They are distinguished from others in the other life, both by their hats, which are black, but of a square form, and flat above...
He afterwards flew out from under my hat - mössa. [NCBS: Swedenborg used the Swedish word mössa here, instead of Latin.]
They were provided with a sharp hat, from which a spike projected.

When I merely thought that I had a fur cap on my head, they were prevented from seeing the interiors of the brain... Presently, good Spirits thinking that they were shut in between that cap and the head... [NCBS: Swedenborg used the Swedish word mössa here, instead of Latin.]
They sit... with a broad whitish reed hat on their heads.
Representation... of a man sleeping with a whitish hat.
There came one from those in the universe. He was a short gross man with a hat which had wool round it.
Concerning certain appearances... such as hats...

If a hat, or cap - mössa, or wig, is taken away from anyone, the communication with such things as inflow from above perishes; so that these articles of clothing are thence. [NCBS: Swedenborg used the Swedish word mössa here, instead of Latin.]
They have a hat or cap down to the eyes, under which as it were they think. [NCBS: Swedenborg used the Swedish word mössa here, instead of Latin.]
By the putting on of garments the communications are varied; especially with hats and turbans; but these are magical things...
A certain one descended thither under the form of a man in a white shirt and a square hat...
